story.headline: Shipowners petition UN over Hormuz tolls
story.summary: Eight global shipping bodies urged the UN to block Strait of Hormuz tolls as Iran and Oman near a deal to jointly manage the waterway.
story.display_body: Eight of the world's largest shipping bodies petitioned the UN on Wednesday 5 August to block any tolls on the Strait of Hormuz, as reports mounted that Iran and Oman are nearing a deal to jointly manage the waterway. In a letter to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the International Maritime Organization — sent Monday 3 August, released publicly Wednesday — the associations warned that charging vessels to transit the strait "would represent a significant departure from established international practice" and could unravel the legal framework governing straits used for international navigation. Roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through Hormuz, which Iran partly controls; separately, Iran's government says it has reached an accord with Oman, which shares the strait's southern shore, on managing traffic there. The move follows months of the US-Israel war on Iran that has repeatedly threatened Gulf shipping.
story.why: A formal toll would be the first attempt to monetize passage through one of the world's most important chokepoints, and any friction there feeds directly into global energy and freight costs — a live risk for import-dependent economies like Switzerland's.

story.headline: Ukraine claims record-depth strike on Russian oil
story.summary: Russian overnight strikes killed at least six in eastern Ukraine while Zelensky claimed a hit on Russian oil facilities over 1,300 km behind the front.
story.display_body: Russian overnight strikes killed at least six people in eastern Ukraine into Thursday 6 August, while Ukraine claimed a record-depth hit on Russian oil infrastructure more than 1,300 km behind the front. Three people died in the Kharkiv region town of Balakliya and three more in the Sumy region, local authorities said; Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 605 Ukrainian drones over its territory and annexed Crimea. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck Russian oil facilities over 1,300 km from the line of contact — among the deepest strikes claimed in the war — as Kyiv presses its campaign against Russian energy exports and Black Sea shipping.
story.why: The deep-strike claim, if confirmed, extends Ukraine's reach well past the front and signals a shift toward attritional pressure on Russia's oil revenue rather than territory.

story.headline: Explosive drone found at Leipzig airport
story.summary: German investigators hunt for a second drone after an explosive-laden drone was found on a Leipzig/Halle runway; the interior minister called it a hybrid attack.
story.display_body: German investigators are hunting for a second drone after an explosive-laden drone was found on a runway at Leipzig/Halle airport, an incident Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called a "hybrid attack scenario" and "a new level of danger." Federal police defused the device, and a team is now searching for parts of a second drone believed to have struck an aircraft in mid-air, DW reported on Thursday 6 August. Dobrindt did not name a culprit, but Western officials have repeatedly accused Russia and its proxies of staging drone incursions and sabotage across Europe.
story.why: An explosive drone at a major cargo hub marks an escalation from the surveillance-style overflights that have unsettled European airports, and it lands as Germany debates how to defend civilian infrastructure against unattributed "grey-zone" attacks.

story.headline: Israel strikes south Lebanon amid Rome talks
story.summary: Israel struck southern Lebanon, accusing Hezbollah of a ceasefire violation, as indirect talks continued in Rome; rights groups sought a war-crimes probe into a journalist's killing.
story.display_body: Israel carried out fresh strikes in southern Lebanon, accusing Hezbollah of a "blatant" ceasefire violation, even as Israeli and Lebanese negotiators continued indirect talks in Rome. The strikes on Wednesday 5 August come with the fragile Lebanon truce under growing strain; separately, Le Monde reported that Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch have called for a war-crimes investigation into the killing of journalist Amal Khalil by the Israeli army in the south.
story.why: Parallel strikes and negotiations underscore how provisional the Lebanon ceasefire remains, and the rights groups' demand raises the stakes over protection of journalists in the conflict.

story.headline: El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate primary
story.summary: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly beat moderate Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, a proxy fight over the party's direction.
story.display_body: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly won Michigan's Democratic Senate primary, results announced 5 August showed, defeating moderate Representative Haley Stevens 48.5% to 47.5% in a contest widely read as a proxy fight over the party's direction. El-Sayed, backed by the party's left wing, will face Republican incumbent Senator Mike Rogers in November for a seat Democrats likely must flip to retake the Senate; President Trump attacked the winner online.
story.why: The razor-thin result is another data point in the Democrats' unresolved progressive-versus-moderate argument heading into a midterm cycle where control of the Senate is at stake.

story.headline: Swiss Post raises letter prices for 2027
story.summary: Swiss Post will raise A- and B-Mail letter prices from January 2027 under a three-year deal with the federal Price Supervisor.
story.display_body: Swiss Post will raise the price of standard letters from the start of 2027, under a three-year deal struck with the federal Price Supervisor (Preisueberwacher). From 1 January 2027, a standard A-Mail letter rises to CHF 1.40 from CHF 1.20, and a B-Mail letter to CHF 1.10 from CHF 1.00; parcel list prices stay frozen through at least end-2029, SRF reported on Thursday 6 August. The agreement, reached after intensive negotiations, covers the period 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2029.
story.why: It is a small but universal cost increase for households and businesses, and it signals how Post is trying to shore up letter-mail revenue as volumes keep falling.

story.headline: Graubuenden demands criminal records from EU citizens
story.summary: Graubuenden's Misox valley now systematically requires criminal-record extracts from EU/EFTA permit applicants, going beyond federal law, as an anti-mafia measure.
story.display_body: The canton of Graubuenden has begun systematically demanding criminal-record extracts from EU/EFTA nationals applying for new residence and cross-border-worker permits in the Misox valley — a check that goes further than federal law allows. The measure, in force at least until year-end, applies to all L, B and G permit applications regardless of concrete suspicion, and the canton justifies it as an anti-organised-crime step, SRF reported on Thursday 6 August. It follows a late-February international police operation in which seven people were arrested, four of them Graubuenden B-permit holders; the lead suspect had been refused a permit by Ticino in 2019 over prior convictions before obtaining one in Graubuenden.
story.why: Applying a blanket screening beyond the federal framework tests the limits of free movement of persons under the EU-Switzerland agreements — precisely the terrain the Bilaterals III talks are meant to stabilise.

story.headline: Confidence in Swiss AHV pension slips
story.summary: A VZ Vermoegenszentrum survey finds declining public trust in Switzerland's AHV state pension even as its share of retirement income grows, while pension-fund confidence recovers.
story.display_body: Public trust in the AHV (Switzerland's first-pillar state pension) is slipping even as its share of retirement income grows, while confidence in occupational pension funds (Pensionskassen) is recovering, a new survey finds. The VZ Vermoegenszentrum's retirement barometer, reported by SRF on Thursday 6 August, shows the AHV — long regarded as the most stable pillar of old-age provision — losing some of that reputation for security, with savers now warming to the second-pillar funds they had been more skeptical of.
story.why: Eroding confidence in the AHV shapes the political weather for pension reform, an issue that keeps returning to the ballot box in Switzerland.

story.headline: Swisscom H1: lower revenue, higher profit
story.summary: Swisscom reported first-half 2026 revenue of CHF 7.2bn, down 3.0% year on year, but higher-than-expected profit after cost cuts.
story.display_body: Swisscom reported first-half 2026 revenue of CHF 7.2 billion, down 3.0% year on year, but delivered higher profit than analysts expected after cost-cutting. The revenue drop stemmed mainly from a 2.1% decline in the core telecom business plus a weaker euro, SRF reported on Thursday 6 August; the group has already raised prices for its main Swisscom brand from April for millions of customers.
story.why: The majority state-owned incumbent is squeezed between competitive pricing pressure and currency effects, and its response — raising consumer prices while cutting costs — bears directly on Swiss telecom bills.
